newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close up but Hansol, Jinro firms fall.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close up but Hansol, Jinro firms fall.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed slightly higher on Friday in a technical rebound in response to the past four straight days of losses, brokers said.
Affiliates of the Hansol and Jinro groups fell. Hansol has been linked in media reports to a scandal involving President Kim Young-sam's son and Jinro is having financial troubles.
Central Banking Corp went limit-up on its largest shareholder's plan to buy more shares in the open market.
The composite index closed up 2.93 points at 687.62.
Analysts said a major market upturn was not expected until investors are assured the economic slump had ended.
"A major rebound of the market will be possible only after investors see concrete signs that the economy has bottomed out," said Shim Choong-bo, research manager at Daishin Securities.
"A sharp rise in exports or a rebound of the Japanese yen (against the dollar) are among major factors that investors are waiting to see," said Shim.
Economists have blamed the weak yen for sluggish exports by South Korean companies, which compete against Japanese makers in most of their key export markets.
Hansol Electron fell 900 won to 21,500 and Hansol Telecommunication shed 1,500 won to 46,500.
Media reports have said the Hansol Group had managed a seven billion won fund on behalf of an associate of President Kim's son, Kim Hyun-chul. Hansol has officially denied the talk.
The Jinro Group has put some of its property and affiliates on sale to raise cash to pay back debt, but no significant progress has yet been reported.
Jinro Ltd was down 220 won to 6,220 and Jinro Industries down 160 won to 4,100.
Yu Sung Co was quoted down 800 won at 9,900, but none of the company's shares was actually traded. Trading in Yu Sung shares resumed on Friday after a two-day suspension.

Yu Sung has been seeking court receivership after defaulting on payments of 337 million won in promissory notes on Tuesday. Brokers said selling orders for Yu Sung shares piled up, but there were no bids to buy.
Central Banking gained 900 won to 12,200 after Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co said it would buy an additional 1.02 million shares in Central to raise its stake.
Shinhan Bank was flat at 10,300 won. On Friday, an additional 3.13 million shares in Shinhan became newly available to foreigner investors.

The additional shares were on top of the uniform 23 percent ceiling set for most South Korean companies. The bid-to-share ratio during the pre-opening bidding for the additional Shinhan shares reached 45.02.

A senior central bank official's remarks commenting on the won/dollar rate trends were ignored. The Bank of Korea official told Reuters the dollar/won rate would stay above the current 890 won level unless the dollar falls further against the yen.
The index futures June contracts fell 0.30 points to 67.85 while the KOSPI-200 index added 0.14 points to 68.57.
--YOO CHOON-SIK (822) 727 5646
